findings.description: Direct cross-account A-to-B retention is refuted for public logout/login: dashboard remounts. A real same-subject access-token refresh does increment ApiClient authMutationEpoch while MainShell cached keys retain the financial State; origin epoch remains stale and later monetary actions block. Include same-claimsVersion refresh in the proposed regression.

Independent execution of the existing retry test passed1/1 EXIT0 and showed a NEW idempotency token after setAuthToken for the same actor. This also occurs on ordinary refresh. A committed partial payment with a lost ACK can therefore be retried with a second key. Stable subject/attempt identity must survive token rotation and app restart; auth epoch is a transport gate only.

Static retry identity map retains failed ambiguous attempts and full observation-bearing fingerprint without a bound. Safe remediation must preserve unresolved tokens; TTL eviction followed by a new token can duplicate a committed partial payment whose ACK was lost and is not accepted as a solution.
